Chapter 7. The Ripple Effect: How the Element Changes Communities.
When someone discovers their Element, the impact hardly ever stops with them alone. You know that feeling—when a person lights up with energy and passion, it’s almost contagious, isn’t it? Suddenly, the excitement they bring to their work, their family, and even their neighborhood, starts to spark change in the people around them.
Sometimes it’s something small—maybe a neighbor starts a book club, or a coworker introduces a fresh idea at the office. But every now and then, these sparks turn into something much bigger.
Picture a small town facing tough times and rising unemployment. Things started to shift when a handful of residents—folks who loved painting, music, and theater—came together to open a community arts center. At first, it was just a few passionate people. But as word got out, more and more joined in. Retirees, teens, parents with little kids—everyone found a place. The center buzzed with life: classes, performances, and a welcoming space for people to connect.
Over time, the entire mood of the town began to change. People felt more hopeful, more invested in each other. Local shops noticed more customers, and new friendships started to form. All of this began with just a handful of residents following their Element.
That arts center? It’s just one example. Think about how this shows up at work. When someone brings their Element to the job, it can spark something in everyone else. Imagine a manager who loves solving problems—suddenly, their team feels encouraged to experiment and take risks. Or a nurse who lights up when teaching others—so they start a mentorship program for new staff. The whole culture shifts, and suddenly, people feel valued for who they are, not just for what they produce.
Most of us don’t realize just how much influence we have. One person, acting from their Element, can totally change the atmosphere of a group. Sometimes, it’s as simple as the way they greet people each morning, or the enthusiasm they bring to a project. Over time, these small gestures add up, creating a sense of possibility that’s hard to ignore.
Communities that nurture the Element—places where people are free to use their strengths—tend to be more resilient. They bounce back from challenges, they find creative solutions together, and people are more likely to step up, help neighbors, or invest in what matters most to everyone.
There’s another story I love: a school struggling with low morale and high turnover. Along comes a new principal, passionate about gardening, who starts a school garden with just a few students. That small garden project grew, drawing in teachers, parents, and even local businesses. Soon, the garden stood as a symbol of renewal, and the whole school culture shifted. Students became more engaged, teachers felt a new sense of support, and suddenly, the community rallied around a shared purpose.
The ripple effect isn’t always dramatic. Sometimes, it’s just the quiet encouragement of a friend, or the steady presence of someone who truly loves what they do. But over time, these moments add up. They create a culture where people feel seen, valued, and inspired to bring their best selves to the table.
